answer:
**Loss of KEAP1 switches on the NRF2 programme** in every cell context that has the knock-down.

The consensus over 5 datasets (4 cell contexts) puts these genes at the top:

| Gene | Meta z | q | Contexts |
|:-----|-------:|--:|---------:|
| NQO1 | 38.2 | 1e-300 | 4 |
| TXNRD1 | 31.7 | 2e-219 | 4 |
| SLC7A11 | 27.4 | 4e-164 | 3 |

What this means:

- The effect is *reproducible*: every gene above is supported in at least 3 contexts.
- In the pathway atlas the knock-down raises `Reactive Oxygen Species Pathway` (meta z 14.9).
- One look-up for a single cell line failed, so there is no per-dataset value here.

Background: KEAP1 targets NRF2 (NFE2L2) for degradation, see [UniProt](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q14145/entry).
